name: Waaree Energies Ltd.
tagline: World's largest non-Chinese solar module maker with 29% ROE, but a Rs 76,000 Cr price already discounts the growth while a sector overcapacity cliff and US anti-dumping duties loom
business_overview: Waaree Energies is India's largest solar PV module manufacturer (group module capacity ~18.7 GW) and the largest non-Chinese module maker globally, now vertically integrating into cells (5.4 GW, TOPCon ramp in H2 FY26), ingots/wafers, plus new legs in energy storage (20 GWh Li-ion cell/battery plan, Rs 10,000 Cr capex), EPC, wind (won a 300 MW Gujarat wind order) and a US manufacturing base. FY26 consolidated revenue rose ~84% to ~Rs 26,537 Cr; order book ~Rs 47,000 Cr (24 GW), ~40% domestic / ~60% overseas.
fundamentals_table: FY26 ~+84% YoY to ~Rs 26,537 Cr; ~44% revenue CAGR (5yr)
fundamentals_narrative: Fundamentally strong today - 29% ROE, 32% ROCE, ~44% revenue CAGR, large multi-year order book, net-cash-like balance sheet. But the stock has already re-rated hugely (52-week high ~Rs 3,864) and at ~Rs 76,000 Cr / ~30x+ earnings, much of the visible FY26-27 growth is priced. The debate is entirely about what happens after FY27-28 when domestic solar-manufacturing capacity (~125 GW built out via PLI) dwarfs ~40 GW domestic demand.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Community references a sharp sector-wide drawdown from Oct 2025 through H1 2026 (Waaree, Waaree Renewable, Premier all falling together), a partial recovery attempt into Aug 2026, and repeated statements that Rs 3,200 was a psychological accumulation zone.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 181 posts (single batch, no escalation), spanning Oct 2025 to Aug 2026. Sentiment swung from euphoria after a record Q2 FY26 concall (EPS doubling YoY, order book raised to Rs 47,000 Cr, GST cut 12%->5% seen as demand-positive, ALMM cell mandate from Jun 2026) into a multi-month slide driven by (1) MNRE signalling a deliberate slowdown of FY26-27 renewable tenders because green-power supply is outstripping grid absorption (~40 GW of projects stuck), (2) an Income Tax Department search across Chikhli/Vapi/Mumbai in Nov 2025, (3) the CMD-level CEO resigning, and (4) the US Commerce Department's April 2026 preliminary anti-dumping/countervailing duty of ~123% on Indian solar cells/panels. Recent posts (Aug 2026) are cautiously constructive: bulls argue the top 4-5 integrated players (Tata Power Solar, Reliance, Adani, Waaree, Premier) will consolidate the market and 'mint money' post-shakeout, that Waaree's US plant keeps it FEOC-compliant, and that quarterly execution + battery/ACC PLI are the next catalysts.
community_signal: No core-tier roster user posted. Elevated-tier karanshah137 posted several times (posts #152, #163, #167) - his stance is nuanced-cautious: overcapacity is a manufacturing-layer 'time bomb' that shows up first in factory utilisation and module prices (from ~FY28), while installers/EPC enjoy a temporary margin super-cycle; he is not making a buy call. Most-loved recent posts (Tushar_Gupta1 11 loves - Q2 concall notes; firefueled 8 loves - 'IT raid is a panic-driven buying opportunity, learnt this from Polycab'; Alvish9031 11 loves - chart only) lean bullish on the panic-as-opportunity framing.
bse_notes: Income Tax Department search operation across Chikhli plant and promoter residences (Nov 2025) - unresolved in the posts read. CEO/CMD-level resignation (Dec 2025-Jan 2026). Subsidiary Waaree Energy Storage Solutions raised Rs 1,003 Cr from strategic investors (Jan 2026). US preliminary AD/CVD duty ~123.04% on Indian solar imports (Apr 2026).
bull_case: 29% ROE / 32% ROCE with ~44% revenue CAGR and an Rs 47,000 Cr (24 GW) order book give real multi-year visibility
Largest non-Chinese module maker with a US manufacturing base - structurally advantaged if US keeps tariffing Chinese/SE-Asian supply and enforcing FEOC rules
Vertical integration into cells/ingots/wafers plus new optionality in 20 GWh battery storage (ACC PLI), EPC and wind diversifies beyond merchant module margins
Bull thesis that the top 4-5 integrated Indian players consolidate the market through the coming glut and emerge with pricing power in 3-4 years
bear_case: At ~Rs 76,000 Cr and ~30x+ earnings the visible FY26-27 growth is already discounted - 10x in 2-3 years would need a ~Rs 7.6 lakh Cr valuation, which is not credible
Sector overcapacity: ~125 GW domestic manufacturing capacity vs ~40 GW domestic demand; multiple community posts expect module prices and factory utilisation - hence margins - to compress from ~FY28
MNRE deliberately slowing FY26-27 renewable tenders due to grid-absorption limits; ~40 GW of projects stuck

US preliminary anti-dumping duty ~123% on Indian solar cells/panels is a direct threat to the ~60% overseas order book (mitigant: US plant, and management says it has not sold India-made cells into the US for 10 years)

Governance overhang: unresolved Nov 2025 Income Tax search; CMD/CEO-level resignation; perception that the juiciest storage assets are being offered to select HNIs/family offices rather than parent shareholders
Rising silver/commodity input costs pressuring module margins
verdict_headline: Genuinely high-quality solar leader, but size plus a well-flagged post-FY28 overcapacity cliff and US tariff risk leave no 10x/2-3yr or 100x/10yr slope
verdict_reasoning: Quality gate is comfortably cleared (29% ROE, 32% ROCE, real ~44% revenue CAGR, strong order book) - this is not a weak-fundamentals filter-out

It is a valuation-and-runway filter-out: at ~Rs 76,000 Cr the known growth is priced, and the community's own consensus is that manufacturing-layer margins compress from ~FY28 as ~125 GW capacity meets ~40 GW demand

US ~123% preliminary anti-dumping duty and the unresolved Nov 2025 IT search are live risks that cap the risk-adjusted upside further; Medium conviction reflects a strong business at a demanding price, not a red flag

four_box.note: Community consensus flags margin compression from FY28 as capacity meets demand, undercutting tailwind; 'known growth is priced' at ~Rs76k Cr.
